title: Find First and Last Position of Element
description: Given an array of integers nums sorted in ascending order, find the starting and ending position of a given target value. If target is not found in the array, return [-1, -1]. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 10^5
nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: The target 8 first appears at index 3 and last appears at index 4.
Target 6 does not exist in the array.

title: Binary Search in Sorted Array
description: Given an array of integers nums sorted in ascending order and an integer target, write a function to search target in nums. If target exists, return its index. Otherwise, return -1. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^4 < nums[i], target < 10^4
All the integers in nums are unique
nums is sorted in ascending order

examples.explanation: 9 exists in nums and its index is 4.
2 does not exist in nums, so return -1.

title: First Bad Version
description: You are given n versions numbered from 1 to n, and you want to find the first bad version, which causes all the following ones to be bad. You are given an integer badVersion representing the first version that is bad (all versions from badVersion to n are bad, all versions before it are good). Given n and badVersion, return the first bad version using a binary search approach (simulate isBadVersion(v) as v >= badVersion).
constraints: 1 <= badVersion <= n <= 2^31 - 1
There is exactly one first bad version
The solution should minimize the number of calls to isBadVersion

examples.explanation: Versions 4 and 5 are bad, versions 1-3 are good. The first bad version is 4.
The only version is bad, so it is the first bad version.

title: Square Root of a Number
description: Given a non-negative integer x, return the square root of x rounded down to the nearest integer. The returned integer should be non-negative as well. You must not use any built-in exponent function or operator such as pow(x, 0.5) or x ** 0.5.
constraints: The result must be an integer (floored square root)
Built-in power/sqrt functions are not allowed
The solution should run in O(log x) time

examples.explanation: The square root of 4 is 2, so the answer is 2.
The square root of 8 is approximately 2.828, and since we round it down, the answer is 2.

title: Find Peak Element
description: A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, find a peak element, and return its index. If the array contains multiple peaks, return the index to any of the peaks. You may imagine that nums[-1] and nums[n] are negative infinity. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(log n) time.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 1000
nums[i] != nums[i + 1] for all valid i
The solution should run in O(log n) time

examples.explanation: 3 is a peak element since it is greater than both its neighbors, so its index 2 is returned.
The value 6 at index 5 is a peak element since it is greater than both its neighbors (5 and 4).
